key_insight: Detonation-spray settings strongly control the trade-off between coating density/roughness, friction, and wear in self-fluxing Ni–Cr–Fe–B–Si–C coatings.
engineering_relevance: The study provides process windows for restoring and strengthening machine parts by tuning spraying parameters to target either lower friction or higher wear resistance.
method: Changed inter-shot delay from 0 to 1 s
evidence_signal: Testing showed the lowest friction at 48% barrel fill and O/C = 1.026 (μ = 0.674 ± 0.136), while the best wear resistance occurred at O/C = 1.856 with 1 s delay, reducing specific wear rate to 0.000189 mm³/(N·m).
watch_item: Lower friction conditions did not necessarily give the best durability, so parameter selection must balance tribology goals against residual-stress-driven cracking and wear.
paper_title: Development of a Method for Producing Self-Fluxing Nickel-Based Coatings by Detonation Spraying
